Figure 2. Culture-Independent Strategies in the Discovery of Novel Natural Products.
This strategy starts with the construction of metagenomic libraries with DNAs extracted from diverse environmental
sources. The libraries are subjected to sequence-based screening for biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) of interest
or function-based screening for clones of interest. Alternatively, the libraries are subjected to metabologenomics
analyses. These strategies open up new opportunities for natural product discovery without the need to isolate
microbial strains.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Pathway Refactoring in the Discovery of Novel Natural Products.
Microbial genome sequences from environmental samples and databases are subjected to bioinformatic analysis
for identiﬁcation of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). BGCs of interest are then assembled by using in vitro DNA
assembly methods. The cassettes may come from the same BGC or multiple BGCs. Heterologous expression of the
refactored BGCs results in the discovery of novel bioactive natural products. Abbreviation: P, promoter.
